newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Prompt fears drive gas oil down.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Prompt fears drive gas oil down.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps gave up all of its early day gains late afternoon and was last quoted down from Thursday as renewed fears of a prompt overhang brought sellers out, traders said on Friday.
"The market is down this afternoon because there are new concerns in the market of more unsold prompt cargoes," one trader said.
July paper was last quoted at $23.15/$23.25, down five cents from Thursday and 20 cents from this morning with the July/August time spread widening to minus 25 cents from 20 cents, brokers said.
July swaps traded earlier in the day at $23.20 while August traded at $23.45 and $23.50, they said.

The prompt overhang has led to one cargo sold earlier in the week at 40 cents below spot quotes against prevailing discounts of about 10 cents. Also one refiner shipped cargoes out for storage outside its refinery complex
Traders said the market is jittery and when a fresh wave of sellers emerge others are also joining in leading to further falls in prices.
The lower prices were despite earlier market optimism after the some buying was seen from China and from traders in the Singapore spot market.

Traders said a floor was set earlier at $23.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for physical cargoes based on the two factors but were unsure if these two players will continue to pick up barrels if they are offered below this mark.
Traders said the Chinese have bought a few 30,000-tonne sized cargoes at around $180 per tonne cost-and-freight basis to south China over the past few days.
The local traders who stepped in to buy spot at $22.90 and $23.00 per barrel on Tuesday are expected to buy more cargoes if prices fall again, traders said.
The traders have since March 3 bought well over 22 million barrels but over the past month have slowed their daily purchases to between one or two 150,000-barrel cargoes or even nothing.

High stocks in Singapore was reflected in data released by the Trade Development Board which showed that middle distillate stocks have risen by 993,000 barrels to 11.236 million barrels for the week ending June 11.
The stocks are at their highest since at least Janaury 1994.
Fuel oil swaps rose slightly on firmer with July indicated at $99.50/$100.50, up 50 cents from Thursday.
Overnight July Brent crude closed up nine cents to $17.44 per barrel and was last traded up 24 cents to $17.68.
